1503.03535_Q03.question: How does Neural Machine Translation (NMT) fundamentally differ from Statistical Machine Translation (SMT) in its approach to optimizing translation probability?
1503.03535_Q03.rag_answer: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) fundamentally differs from Statistical Machine Translation (SMT) in its approach to optimizing translation probability by directly optimizing the log-probability of the target translation \( p(y|x) \) using a single neural network. In contrast, SMT systems decompose the optimization into a language model \( p(y) \) and a translation model \( p(x|y) \), fitting them separately using a log-linear model that combines multiple features. NMT integrates feature extraction and normalization into a single neural network, allowing for end-to-end training. To optimize the joint probability, NMT employs an encoder-decoder framework, where the encoder converts the source sentence into a continuous-space representation, and the decoder generates the target translation.
